name: MN-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+18 district fundamentals strongly favor Democrats
McCollum's roughly 24-to-1 fundraising advantage and $500K+ cash on hand
Challenger Wikstrom is minimally funded with no outside support
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%
model.rationale: The St. Paul-area seat's eighteen-point Democratic lean, McCollum's two-decade incumbency, and an overwhelming financial edge leave Wikstrom without a visible path; markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
model.watch: Only a late scandal or a surge of outside spending against McCollum could put the outcome in doubt, and neither has materialized.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Minnesota's fourth district, centered on St. Paul and its eastern suburbs, carries a partisan lean of about eighteen points toward Democrats. Betty McCollum has held the seat since 2001 and is running again. Republican Paul Wikstrom advances to the general election with minimal resources.

The financial gap is stark: McCollum has raised about $1.5 million and holds more than $500,000 on hand, while Wikstrom has raised roughly $65,000 with under $20,000 available, and no outside groups are spending on either side. No public polling of the general election exists, and no national race raters have flagged the contest as competitive, though prediction markets put Democratic odds near ninety-six percent. Fundamentals, money, and incumbent history all point to a comfortable McCollum re-election, with the real question being the size of her margin rather than who wins.
